checks.evidence: B1 and B4 are applied. tastemaker-core now requires idiomatic-sh-ryo-sdk 0.1.2 (crates/tastemaker/crates/core/Cargo.toml:33), and the seal's three doc comments state exactly what it enforces: every MatchingUseCase implementation, in any crate, gains PatternSemantics through the bridge, and no type implements it directly (execution_domain domain/matching/types.rs:11-27). The new tm types Scope and ScopeKind (imports/types.rs:81-99) and the Name.binding field are crate-internal domain data in an unpublished-at-this-version crate. sdk/api.txt is unchanged. An advisory notes that the cli manifest still asks for SDK 0.1.1.

ScopeKind is an enum the match in keep() maps from the two kind strings, and any other kind is not kept (import_rows/service.rs:102-113). Relation::Scopes is a new variant, so both matches over Relation (query, keep) are exhaustive by construction. No test stands in for a type.

F5 (being fixed under its own item): Tastemaker's cold check of crates/ryo peaks at 4,491,136 KiB against its 1,331,200 KiB guard. It is red only with the tm import-reading branch's core changes (validation.json tastemaker_workspace; gatefix_tastemaker_without_tm_branch.log). The scope logic shows why. (a) The new built-in rule SCOPES (import_rows/constants.rs:38-41) selects from syntax-tree with glob_any(kind, "{stmt-list,item-list}"), so it emits a row for every block and every item list of every file: every function body, impl body and trait body, not only those around a use. A glob is not a kind equality, and only an initial run of total kind equalities narrows dispatch (execution_domain shared_walk/service.rs). Every one of those rows goes back to Tastemaker as a lint answer with its columns, and is then copied into a Scope holding its own RepoPath (import_rows/service.rs:108-112, imports/types.rs:83-90). (b) imports() runs in_scope for each use-site edge against each name whose binding matches, and in_scope scans all of the file's scopes twice (service.rs:147-169). It recomputes the innermost scope of the same use for every edge, which is O(edges x scopes) per file. Only (a) is a plausible cause of a 3.2 GB increase; (b) is CPU.

Scope is a projection of the engine's syntax-tree answer into Tastemaker's own row type, the same way Name, Package and Owner already project their relations (imports/types.rs). No second definition of an existing Tastemaker concept is added. EDGES_RELATION and EDGE_KEY, left unused by the early return, are deleted (constants.rs).
No dependency is added. The Cargo.lock change is only tastemaker's own version going from 0.1.1 to 0.1.2 (crates/tastemaker/Cargo.lock:1549,1590).

F6 (being fixed under its own item): core application::reporting::service_test::succeeds is red, with 0 findings where 1 is expected (service_test.rs:492, gatefix_tastemaker_workspace.log:7960). The cause is a real behaviour change, not just the test. keep() now drops any static-import row without a binding cell: it matches if let (Some(written), Some(binding)) (import_rows/service.rs:73-82). The test's answer has target and span but no binding, so its import is no longer read. The same drop hits production rows: the JavaScript provider gives a side-effect import and a dynamic import(..) an unknown binding (languages/javascript/src/domain/syntax/service.rs:272, :291-292), so such imports stop reaching the import rules, a silent false negative. F7 (pending, a later delta): the two replay samples rows of go/api went red at 332 through the local ryo crates the patch links; they are green at 331. F8: the two tm production fixes, 55e5fd3520 and e2c66a218a, name no test in their commit messages and have no red_green entry (validation.json still holds 30). Their service_test cases exist (a_path_at_a_use_site_through_a_name_an_import_binds_is_that_imports, a_path_in_an_inline_module_sees_no_import_written_outside_it and four others) but are not shown failing without the fixes.

The delta adds no unsafe, no #[allow], and no unwrap, expect or panic in production. in_scope's size() maps an unplaced scope to usize::MAX on purpose, so that scope never wins as the innermost (service.rs:148-151). The std::sync::atomic::* allow-list entry (crates/ryo/tastemaker.toml:205) is justified: the providers' production code already uses it (python parse/contract.rs, ruff_python_parser adapter.rs and semantic.rs).
